hints: A path can cross many heavy-light chains, but each chain segment is contiguous in the flattened order.
Decompose the tree into heavy paths so each root-to-node route crosses only logarithmically many chains.
Use a segment tree for each flattened path range and climb the deeper chain head until both nodes share one chain.
analogy: Split a tree path into a small number of straight array intervals, then query each interval.
example: If u and v lie on different chains, query the deeper chain head to its node, move to its parent, and repeat.
algorithm: Build heavy-light decomposition and a max segment tree over base positions. For path query, repeatedly query the deeper head-to-node segment, climb above that head, then query the final same-chain interval; point updates change one base position.
correctness: Heavy-light decomposition partitions the unique u-v path into disjoint chain intervals; taking their maximum yields exactly the path maximum.
complexity: O(log^2 n) per query/update and O(n) space.
